title: Should I buy an investment condo now, or save 12 years for my dream landed home?
excerpt: A 33-year-old father earning RM10,000 wonders whether to buy an investment condo or save until his late 40s for a corner terrace. Sean says prices will outrun his savings, so buy a unit the rent can carry.

question.asker: From Mr N, a viewer who wrote in by email
question.context: Mr N, 33, takes home about RM10,000 a month, has two young children and lives with his parents. After insurance, a car loan, a RM2,700 housing loan, food, his mother's allowance and other costs he has about RM2,500 left each month, plus about RM75,000 in crypto. He is weighing a studio or two-room condo of up to RM700,000 as an investment in 2024 against saving for 12 years to buy a corner terrace house in Kwasa Land or Elmina in his late 40s.
question.text: Should he buy an investment property now despite his budget, or keep saving for his dream landed home?

answer.quote: I think the proposition here is to own the apartment first.
answer.summary: Buy an investment unit first, but a smaller one than RM700,000: an instalment of about RM2,000 to RM2,500, on a unit where current rents already cover it. Let it build equity for 10 to 12 years, then sell it for the down payment on the terrace house, instead of chasing prices with savings alone.

reasons.title: Savings rarely catch property prices
reasons.body: Elmina Green homes launched at about RM600,000 to RM700,000, and later phases cost about RM1.2 million. A friend of Sean's saved for years for a Shah Alam terrace as its price kept moving out of reach.

reasons.title: A RM4,000 instalment is too much stress
reasons.body: His income could get a loan of about RM1 million, but a RM4,000 instalment with two children leaves no room if the unit sits empty or his job changes. About RM2,000 to RM2,500 a month is his sweet spot, roughly a RM500,000 to RM600,000 unit.

reasons.title: Build in a safety factor
reasons.body: Choose a unit where rents nearby already cover the instalment, so it still works if rents fall 10% by completion. And budget about RM50,000 for furnishing so it can be let as soon as the keys arrive.

reasons.title: Crypto isn't a plan
reasons.body: Money in crypto should be money he can afford to lose overnight, not the foundation for a home.

actions: Set your instalment limit at about RM2,000 to RM2,500 a month and search for units at that price.
Check current rents for each shortlisted unit, and make sure a 10% drop still covers the instalment.
Save bonuses towards a furnishing budget of about RM50,000 for handover.
With little time for research, consider paying for professional deal sourcing and data.
Plan to sell the unit in 10 to 12 years to fund the down payment on your terrace house.
caveat: This depends on his job staying secure; if it doesn't, a smaller unit or waiting is safer. Sean points to a bulk purchase club he is a VIP member of and buys from, which he says he doesn't run.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #219. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer and Sean stated them in August 2023. Sean recommends a property investment club he is a VIP member of and buys from.
